recipes.name: Root Beer Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 3 (12 fluid ounce) cans or bottles root beer

steps.text: Place the pork chops in a dish; pour 2 cans of the root beer over the chops. Place in refrigerator to marinate at least 2 hours. Remove the pork chops from the root beer; season with salt and pepper.

Combine the remaining can of root beer, the beef stock, brown sugar, hot sauce, and Worcestershire sauce in a saucepan over medium heat; simmer the mixture until it reduces to about 3/4 cup. Set aside.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat, and lightly oil the grate.

Grill the pork chops on the preheated grill until the no longer pink in the center, about 8 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Brush the chops generously with the reduction sauce and continue cooking for about 2 minutes more per side. Remove from grill and brush with any remaining sauce. Season with salt to taste before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Root Beer Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Pork chops are marinated in root beer and then glazed with a reduction of root beer, beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, and brown sugar while on the grill for a simple and tasty main dish.

video.description: These are great for outdoor grilling. Simple and very tasty. The glaze at the end gives them a lot of concentrated flavors.

review.reviewBody: I will agree somewhat with WERFLY. This was written toward my some of my families tastebuds (which can be a little wimpy at times). That's the one I submitted. I prefer it marinated all day with the rootbeer and a tablespoon of worchestershire, heavily salted/peppered prior to grilling. 2 teaspoons chipotle sauce and I also use Campbells 2x strength beef broth to start for this. The reduction down to 3/4 cup is approximate (I tend not to measure things-rather go by taste), it should be pretty potent and salty sweet. Remember, you have to taste everything and make sure to adjust seasoning to your families tastes.

Oh YEAH. Seasoned the chops with a salt-free seasoning blend before soaking in the root beer. Reduced the root beer from the marinade along with the extra, used 1 beef boullion cube and "red hot" sauce (no chipotle), brown sugar, and the worcestershire. Had to strain out some solids and reduced it down to about a 1/4C (for 4 chops), so it took a while, but the reduction syrup was worth it. Peppered the chops and lightly salted with seasoned salt before grilling on the Foreman. Yum, Yum YUM. Great way to use up some root beer that had went flat. ;)

Full disclosure, I was surprised by this recipe. Really easy and - the surprise - really delicious. I paired it with onions and mushrooms cooked and then soaked in remaining root beer over heat until the root beer had largely reduced and caramelized. Well received. No leftovers.

I made the following changes and it was amazing!

-Marinated overnight and added worcestershire sauce to the marinate
-Cooked chops in cast iron skillet (added liquid smoke to get that grill flavor) 
-Used Sriracha instead of chipotle sauce
-Added a corn starch slurry to sauce to help it thicken

This was awesome. My husband gave it an A+. Two things: (1) It took longer than I thought to make the reduction (more than 30 min!), so I turned up the heat and this helped. It was also the first time I've made a reduction, so I can blame inexperience. (2) When it was reduced enough in volume, it was still too runny. So I added a couple of teaspoons of cornstarch and heated until it made a nice glaze. I don't have a grill, so I broiled the porkchops and basted with the glaze. I served them over rice with extra glaze on top and green beans. The porkchops were tender and not dry. Very tasty! Thanks for sharing this recipe!

Great recipe! I made a few adjustments as recommended by Ken’s suggestions in his feedback/ratings—increased the amount of both the Worcestershire sauce and chipotle sauce in the glaze, and added both of these ingredients to the marinade mix. Our family of 5 picky kids and my husband all said these were the absolute best pork chops they had ever had, and begged me to make them again. A definite keeper!

Keeper - Really good flavor. 
I cooked the sauce down to thick or ~ 1 cup. 
Also added W sauce and 1 t garlic powder to root beer for marinade and let sit overnight. 
Used sriracha instead.

I made this twice with tenderloin rather than chops. First time per the recipe and it was good. The second time I added a shot of Worcestershire, a chopped chipotle and ground pepper to the marinade which stayed in the bag for 8 hours. Using my favorite go to, Tuong Ot Sriracha chili sauce in the glaze rather than chipotle, I reduced it to 1/4 and brushed it on the last 5 minutes of grill time and on the final 1 inch slices when plated. Wow! This it's a keeper now!

This was a hit with my family. I read some of the other reviews saying that they thought it was a little bland. Since I cook for 3 hungry teenagers and a husband who like it spicy, I generally double up on all the ingredients and triple or quadruple the heat factor. I found that using 4 tablespoons of chopped chipotle peppers and it gave it just enough kick. I paired it with a good Parmesan smashed potato. Will definitely be making again.
This was a yummy recipe! My whole family liked it. I am on a low-carb diet, so I used diet root beer and substituted Sukrin Gold for the brown sugar.
I liked the glaze but my pork chops were dry. Next Time wrap the chops in foil and cook them wrapped.
Love this recipe!

This recipe reinforced two things. 1-pour root beer into a glass over ice cream and enjoy! 2-if you want a tender pork chop, bake them at low temp (250 degrees) for a couple hours. Then grill, fry or finish them to your preference. Seemed to me like this was a lot of effort for a tough chop!
I would give less than 1 star if I could. What a waste of pork chops, root beer and money.
My kids loved it. The sauce reduction took some time and turned out fantastic.
THE WORST. Followed directions precisely. Marinade never reduced to be "gooey." Dried out, tasteless. Not for me.
I let them marinate overnight and they were juicy
okay nothing special

I wish I could give this recipe 10 stars!!!! Absolutely amazing. I must admit that at first I did not get marinating the pork chops in root beer but I assure that it more than works!!! I rate a recipe my saying if it’s company worthy and this one is!!!
